items.title: NEW — CONTEXT-REACHABILITY diagnostics CASCADE behind a resolution error: on kolt at d783fbf4 with its seven retired `View` methods still written, `vilan check` reported 180 errors — 7 real (A99's steer) and 173 `context \`owner_scope\` is read here, but this code can be reached without an enclosing \`run\`` (146), `required by …'s \`context\` clause` (10), `reads context …, so it can't be used as a value` (9) and one injected-closure error, 74 of them in the generated lucide module that writes no closure at all; migrating the seven sites took the count to 1. Mechanism: a closure handed to a call that failed to resolve never attaches to the clause-carrying parameter it was written for, so every function it reaches (the pages, the icons, everything under them) is reachable 'without an enclosing run' along that path — one primary error fans out into every context read downstream of the closure
items.discussion: the owner (2026-09-15): 'investigate the ridiculous amount of context requirement diagnostics. Perhaps the context diagnostics shouldn't appear at all if there are other diagnostic kinds present?' REC: the narrow rule first — a reachability path that passes through an UNRESOLVED call (or a closure argument of one) contributes nothing to the walk (the path's premise failed), which kills this cascade at its root and keeps context errors on a program whose only defect is the missing `run`; the owner's broad rule — suppress the context family outright while any resolution/type error is present in the program — as the backstop the narrow rule does not reach (a closure typed by a failed call elsewhere), the way unused-import fades already go silent under any diagnostic
items.body: context.rs: the reachability walk (`analyze`'s reach edges) skips edges whose call failed to resolve and closures that are arguments of such calls; then the program-level gate: `context` family diagnostics dropped when the diagnostics list already carries a resolution/type error (a note on the first primary error saying context checks were skipped). Pins: the kolt shape (a retired method taking a closure whose body reaches a context read — one error, not two); the pure missing-`run` program still errors; the broad gate's pin (a type error elsewhere + a genuine missing run → the run error is deferred, the note says so).

items.title: NEW — the never-silent body-less-emission refusal (B55, `internal: a call resolved to \`Slot\`'s requirement \`place\`, which has no body …`) carries NO usable span: its span is the trait requirement's name in std, which the CLI never renders, so kolt showed one bare `Error:` line with no file, no line and no hint which of 19 files to look in; the emitter at that point does not know the call site either (`function_with_name` records the bodyless id when the requirement is EMITTED, long after the call that asked for it). The integrator had to instrument `ensure_function_emitted` to learn the emitting stack (`app_shell` → `place`) and bisect kolt by hand
items.discussion: the integrator's find on kolt at d783fbf4 (2026-09-15), while chasing B351
items.body: Record, with the bodyless id, the function being emitted when the requirement was first requested (`ensure_function_emitted`'s caller: `self.emitting`'s innermost + `current_admitting_file`) and the call expression id if the resolver has it; the message names the function and its file, and the span is the CALL's when known, the enclosing function's name otherwise; a pin over B351's reproduction asserts the file and line.

items.title: NEW — REGRESSION (Order 36): a block hole whose tail is `context.run(v, \|\| { <element .child(swap(s, \|x\| match x { .. => <e/>, .. => <div .child(swap(t, \|y\| match y { .. })) /> })) /> })` leaves `run<U>`'s `U` unresolved, and the emitter reaches `Slot::place` with no body — the B55 internal refusal, on a shape kolt compiled at 9b22ec36 (its `app_shell`). Twenty-line reproduction at the integrator's scratch `kolt-migrate/run-repro/src/client.vl` (case h): the same program with `run` replaced by a user generic `ident<U>(body: \|\| U): U` PASSES, with an expression-bodied closure PASSES, with a single (un-nested) `swap` PASSES, outside a `{{ }}` block hole PASSES, with both closure parameters annotated PASSES — the trigger needs the EXTERNAL generic `run`, a block-bodied closure, and a nested `swap` whose `C` is decided by `match` arms. Workaround in kolt (views.vl:89, FIXME): `let shell: View = user_context.run(..); shell`
items.discussion: the integrator's find on kolt at d783fbf4 (2026-09-15); culprit lane: bisect in progress (49611256 before lang-b vs 365dd9ff after — B333's closure landings and B340's coercion note both touch `infer_type_inner`; B347 is the sibling) — stamped when known
items.body: Bisect to the commit; the fix is where the closure's return type is seeded for an external generic's closure parameter (B333's `adoptable_closure`/`call_return_clause` or B340's `note_callable_coercion` gate in `infer_type_inner`); pin the reproduction and the four passing variants; drop kolt's FIXME at the owner's word.
